Another Reshuffle

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Yet another cabinet reshuffle for our besieged president - and some surprising moves, but what does it all mean?

Unique Selling Point:
President Zuma this morning reshuffled his cabinet for the umpteenth time. And while some might say the axing of Blade Nzimande was a foregone conclusion after the SACP's open attack on the president over the past few months, the appointment of former State Security Minister David Mahlobo to the energy portfolio has set tongues wagging. So what does it all mean? Will the appointment of Zuma loyalist Mahlobo help secure the nuclear deal for Zuma? And will this be the last straw for the SACP and the the tri-partheid alliance, as many commentators are calling the firing of Nzimande an act of all out war.

Summary:
We delve behind the headlines and unpack the deeper meaning of the latest reshuffle. Is this a last ditch effort by the president to secure lucrative deals for himself and his ANC faction, and an open admonishment of the SACP? Or will the appointment of Buti Manamela appease the SACP. Why, despite lots of speculation, has Dlamini-Zuma not been made a minister? And what does the appointment of ANC MP Bongani Bongo (who only became an mp in 2014) to the powerful head of state security position spell for the country?

Press Release:


Reshuffling the Cards
On Tuesday morning, embattled President Jacob Zuma once again reshuffled his cabinet, firing
the SACP’s Blade Nzimade. While some analysts say the axing of Nzimande was a foregone
conclusion after the SACP openly called for Zuma to resign from office; the appointment of former
State Security Minister David Mahlobo to the Energy portfolio has set tongues wagging. A
declaration of war against the SACP or a President backed into a corner? Carte Blanche analyses
the political fallout

Script:


Another Reshuffle
20 Oct 2017

Voice
It’s been a busy time in South African politics with President Jabob Zuma finally appointing a new SABC board, a new SAA board and axing Dudu Myeni, the chairperson of the embattled airline. But one of the biggest surprises came earlier this week.

Link Devi
On Tuesday morning while South Africans went about their business President Jacob Zuma dropped yet another bombshell when he reshuffled his cabinet for the 12th time since 2009.

Voice
This was the second cabinet shake up this year, after a midnight reshuffle in March, which saw the removal of then finance minister Pravin Gordhan and his deputy Mcebisi Jonas. Political analyst Prof Tinyiko Maluleke says its par for the course for the Zuma presidency.

Sound Up Prof Tinyiko Maluleke
Prof: This is Zuma’s style. Zuma has managed to create instability again and again. Especially around the people who work with him.

Voice
The two most note worthy changes came with the axing of Minister of Higher Education and Training Blade Nzimande and the moving of former minister of State Security David Mahlobo to the Energy portfolio.

Sound Up Prof Tinyiko Maluleke
To begin with I think this is Zuma saying I am still in charge. So it’s a message to all his detractors, it’s a message to the country, to say that you know regardless of all the court rulings and all of that I am still able.

Voice
The full list of changes looks like this. Hlengiwe Mkhize is the new Minister of Higher Education and Training, with the SACP’s Buti Manamela her new deputy.. Mmamoloko Kubayi heads up communications, David Mahlobo is minister of Energy, Ayandla Dlodlo moves to Home Affairs, and newcomer Bongani Bongo gets the coveted State Security portfolio.

Sound Up Prof Tinyiko Maluleke
But I think it’s also a chilling message to cabinet ministers, that if you don’t do what I tell you to do you can go anytime.

Voice
The latest reshuffle saw blowback from across the political landscape, with the SACP furious at the removal of its General Secretary Blade Nzimande, calling it a direct attack on the party.

Sound Up
We emphatically reject these maneuvers that place the alliance on the brink of disintegration. Our view is that this is not a reshuffle, but the targeted removal of comrade Blade as a direct attack on the SACP.

Voice
The axing of Nzimande has been the subject of much speculation over the past few months as the SACP have repeatedly called for Zuma to step down. General Secretary of the South African Federation of Trade Unions, SAFTU, Zwelinzima Vavi says the president is punishing Nzimande for not towing the line.

Sound Up Zwelinzima Vavi
I’m sure he’s very angry at Blade Nzimande. He wants to show him who is the boss around. He doesn’t care about the alliance, he doesn’t care about anything else except the family, so Blade Nzimande will taste the bitter medicine that many other have tasted before.

Voice
While many analysts have questioned whether the move will finally see the Communist Party leave the Tri-Partheid alliance, Vavi says the alliance has been dead in the water for a long time.

Sound Up Vavi
Vavi: The alliance is long gone. I mean we were kicked out with Numsa for pointing out that there is no alliance in the practical sense. The alliance program is one.

Devi: You guys said that when?

Vavi: 2013, 2012, if you go to the secretariat report that Blade Nzimande and others were gunning for. It is because we were speaking the truth then that there is no alliance.

Voice
According to research the average Zuma cabinet lasts only 8.6 months, raising concerns about the stability of government. A view conceded by ANC Treasurer General and presidential contender Zweli Mkhize.

Sound Up Zweli
The concern would be about any impression of instability that might arise, and I think those issues are issues that require leadership to look at.

Voice
Former Minister of Intelligence Ronnie Kasrils says South Africa might end up in the record books

Sound Up Ronnie Kasrils
It must be a world record. I can’t think of any country where you have reshuffles on this kind of basis. And of course, it’s very destabilizing for government.

Voice
Kasrils says President Zuma is doing his own ministers an injustice by not allowing them sufficient time to get to grips with their portfolios.

Sound Up Ronnie Kasrils
I’ve been a minister, 14 year period, it takes a good couple of years of one’s term to really get to know the ropes and settle in and get on top of things.

Voice
While speculation continued about the motives behind Zuma’s latest moves, firebrand Julius Malema had this message for the president.

Sound Up Julius Malema
We don’t care about these delays and all that, Zuma will be in prison as a pensioner. He must know that. It doesn’t matter how long it takes for the EFF to take power, all these thugs are going to go to jail.

Link Devi
The appointment of pro-Zuma cadre David Mahlobo to the energy portfolio seems to further entrench the belief that President Jacob Zuma will push for a nuclear deal with Russia whether we can afford it or not.

Sound Up Vavi
Devi: But why do you think a reshuffle now, two months before the December conference?

Vavi: The nuclear must be delivered. The Russians should be knocking at the door to say, you guys said that you are in charge, demonstrate that you are in charge. And therefore you can’t wait for December. More so, no one can predict with certainty what will happen in December. There’s a trillion rand at stake in relation to the nuclear build up program, they need it.

Voice
The suspicions are well founded says energy expert Chris Yelland, especially considering that South Africa is in the midst of an energy crisis as the Eskom saga drags on, we’re still awaiting the long overdue Integrated Energy Plan and we’ve seen three new ministers this year alone.

Sound Up Chris Yelland
I was astounded by the appointment of the minister of State Security into a portfolio like energy. This year alone we’ve had three ministers of energy. Minister Joemat-Petterson, Minister Kubaji and now Minister Mahlobo. So it’s really difficult for a newcomer, especially one with absolutely no background in energy to get to grips with this new portfolio.

Voice
But, unlike many analysts, Yelland says pro-nuclear cabinets will not guarantee that the nuclear deal will go ahead.

Sound Up Chris
Devi: There has been the observation that this could be a pro nuclear cabinet?

Chris: It may be, and it would appear so from the statements that the new minister has made, but I have a different take on this matter.

Voice
In May this year the Western Cape High Court set aside all nuclear deals South Africa had entered into, a decision that then Minister of Energy Mmamoloko Kubayi did not challenge.

Sound Up Chris
And honestly, if Eskom or the Department of Energy try and proceed in defiance of this court judgment they will be before the courts very quickly again.

Link Devi
The State Security Ministry is an incredibly important arm of government. It’s responsible for the safekeeping of South Africa and its citizens. The minister of intelligence has to be a highly trusted individual in a world where trust is in short supply.

Sound Up Ronnie Kasrils
And he’s appointed again, someone – advocate Bongo, who’s been a backbench MP, with no connection to this portfolio whatsoever.

Voice
Advocate Bongani Thomas Bongo became an MP in 2014, and has served on portfolio committees for Justice and Correctional services as well as the Joint Standing Committee on Defence.

Sound Up Bongani Bongo
So I feel very honored that the president invited me to come and assist in the capacity that he requested me to assist on.

Sound Up Kasrils
You have to have someone who can lay the law down. And make it clear to those who are in the services that we play by the rules. We’ve got these huge responsibilities and power that must not be abused.

Devi: Cyril Rhamaphosa, is he on thin ice?

Voice
Some analysts say this might not be the last reshuffle on the cards, as many people expected to see Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma in cabinet after she was appointed an mp earlier this year.

Sound Up Prof Maluleke
Devi: The other theory is that Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma is biding her time because she’s got to prepare for the election race in December?

Prof: You see this is the genius of Zuma. He makes us all keep wondering what his motivations are for including this one and not that one he makes all cabinet ministers lie awake at night, and wonder if they are next or not.

Devi: Cyril Rhamaphosa, is he on thin ice?

Prof: Well you know Cyril must never relax, in my view. He must not make the mistake of thinking that the presidency is in the bag, ever. Not until the fat lady sings.

Voice
The presidency did not respond to our repeated requests for comment. But in the run up to the ANC’s elective conference in December, we can expect more drama for those in the halls of power. And it remains to be seen if President Zuma will hold office until the end of his term in 2019. But for many, that day can’t come soon enough.

Sound Up Vavi
The president always acts strictly on the basis of advancing his personal, family, friends, crony capitalist surroundings of himself – nothing else. There’s no country in the equation, no ANC, no alliance, nothing else. Only the family and the friends.
